column1: # POSIX external provider manifest — the commands the Go multicall does not implement.
# LICENSE POSTURE (this is why the file is shaped this way):
# Every provider below is COPYLEFT — GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, or the Vim license. None
# is permissive. Building these and hosting the BINARIES would make this project
# a distributor and trigger GPLv3 s6 / GPLv2 s3: convey corresponding source,
# build scripts and installation information, for every artifact, indefinitely.
# So build and download are deliberately SEPARATED:
#   download -> UPSTREAM source only, pinned by sha256. Upstream is the
#               distributor; its obligations are already discharged.
#   build    -> LOCAL, from the recipe in build.sh. A binary you build for
#               yourself is not distribution, so no obligation is triggered.
#   we ship  -> this manifest and the recipe. Our own work, our own license.
# Never mirror or republish the built binaries. If an organisation chooses to
# host an internal prebuilt mirror, that is ITS distribution and it must ship
# the corresponding source alongside; this project does not.
# VERSIONS are pinned to exactly what the Profile A/B reference host runs, so a
# Profile C arm differs from A only in WHO supplies the command, never in which
# implementation. Re-pin only together with the reference image.
# sha256 is of the upstream artifact as downloaded, verified before extraction.
# An entry without a digest is REFUSED, never built.
